1.1: This right here? The Song of Songs—Solomon's masterpiece. The one that outshines 'em all.
1.2: Baby, I want him to kiss me—kiss me deep. 'Cause your love? Sweeter than the finest wine.
1.3: You smell good, real good—like expensive oil flowin' through the room. Your name? Whew. Your name alone smell like legacy. That's why the women all got love for you.
1.4: Take me with you. Pull me close. The King took me to his room—and it was more than I imagined. We gon' rejoice in you! Your love? Better than wine. No wonder folks out here celebratin' you. They love you for real—and they ain't wrong.
1.5: I may be dark, but I'm still fine. O daughters of Jerusalem, don't get it twisted. I'm like the bold tents of Kedar, like Solomon's royal curtains—rich, layered, and strong.
1.6: Don't judge me by my skin tone. The sun been kissin' me. My brothers stayed mad at me, had me workin' in the fields, but I ain't even get to take care of my own self—my own 'vineyard.'
1.7: Tell me where you be, my love—where you lead your flock, where you rest around noon. I don't wanna be out here wanderin' like some stranger, lookin' lost around your people.
1.8: If you don't know where I be, queen of beauty, just follow the tracks. Walk with the flock, tend to your lil goats near the shepherd tents.
1.9: Girl, you remind me of a royal stallion—one of Pharaoh's finest. You strong, sleek, powerful.
1.10: Your cheeks glisten with jewelry, and your neck? Laced in gold. You shine different.
1.11: We gon' hook you up with custom gold, sis—with silver studs to match your shine.
1.12: While my man sittin' at the table, my perfume fillin' the whole room. He got me activated.
1.13: He like a bundle of myrrh I keep close—layin' on my chest, restin' with me all night.
1.14: He like a bouquet of henna blossoms—fresh outta En Gedi. A rare, sacred scent. Ain't nothin' common 'bout him.
1.15: Look at you, my love… just look. You so beautiful. Your eyes soft like doves.
1.16: And you? Whew, you fine-fine. Pleasant in every way. Our bed lush and green—like new beginnings.
1.17: The beams above us? Cedar strong. The rafters? Fir wood. Solid. This love? It's built to last.

2.1: I'm the rose from out in Sharon—the lily still standin' in the valley low.
2.2: Girl, you like a lily growin' between thorns—that's how you stand out from all the others.
2.3: And you? You like an apple tree in a forest of plain oaks—you the one who stand tall and give shade. I sat under you feelin' safe and sweet. Your fruit? Whew, it tasted like joy.
2.4: He took me to his celebration table—and his banner over me? It said 'Love.'
2.5: Bring me raisin cakes. Hand me apples. I'm weak with love. I'm lovesick for real.
2.6: His left arm cradled my head, his right hand held me close. Whew...
2.7: So I'm tellin' y'all—O daughters of Jerusalem—swear it by the gazelles or the does in the field: Don't push love too fast. Don't wake it 'til it's ready.
2.8: I hear him—my man's voice! He comin'! Jumpin' hills, runnin' through mountains like he floatin'.
2.9: My baby like a gazelle, a young buck movin' smooth. Now he peekin' through the window, gazin' through the screen like he can't wait no more.
2.10: He called to me, sayin'—'Come on now, my love. My fine one, get up. Let's go.'
2.11: The cold days over. Rain gone, sky clear.
2.12: Flowers poppin' up everywhere, birds singin' like the world just woke up. The doves? They cooing all soft in the breeze.
2.13: Fig trees got baby fruit, and the vines smellin' real sweet. Come on, baby—let's go.
2.14: My dove, you be hidin' like you in a cliff or tucked in a rock. But I wanna see your face. I wanna hear that voice. You sound like peace, and you look like art.
2.15: Y'all, help us catch the little foxes—the ones messin' up the vineyard. Our love still fresh, still tender—don't let nothin' come through and ruin it.
2.16: My man is mine, and I'm his. He movin' through the lilies, feeding what's his.
2.17: 'Til the morning light breaks in and shadows slip away—come back to me, my love. Come like a gazelle, come like that young stag and meet me up in the mountains of longing.

3.1: That night, layin' in my bed, I reached for him—the one my soul loves. I looked, but he wasn't there.
3.2: I said, 'Nah, I gotta get up. I'ma hit these streets, search every block, every alley, 'til I find my love.' But still—I couldn't find him.
3.3: Then the city guards came by, walkin' their night shift. I stopped 'em like, 'Y'all seen him? The one I love?'
3.4: Barely walked past them, and boom—I found him. Grabbed him tight, held him close, wouldn't let go for nothin'. I brought him to my mama's house, to the same room I came from—yeah, that deep.
3.5: And again I tell y'all, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and the soft-eyed deer: Don't push love too soon. Don't wake it 'til it's good and ready.
3.6: Wait—who that comin' out the wilderness? Movin' like smoke columns risin' in the air, scented with myrrh, frankincense, and every fine cologne money can buy?
3.7: That's Solomon's ride—his royal couch, surrounded by sixty of Israel's strongest—men who don't play when it comes to protection.
3.8: They all strapped, trained for battle, swords tight to they thighs—'cause even love needs security in the dark hours.
3.9: Solomon ain't ride basic—he had a whole chariot built outta Lebanon wood.
3.10: Pillars made of silver, base of gold, seats draped in royal purple. Inside? Laid with love—crafted by the sisters in Jerusalem.
3.11: Step out, daughters of Zion—come see this. Look at King Solomon rockin' the crown his mama set on his head, back when he got married—on the happiest day of his life.

4.1: Girl, you fine, for real. Like, breathtaking. Your eyes behind that veil? Dove-like—soft and deep. Your hair fall like a whole flock of goats cascading down Mount Gilead.
4.2: Your teeth? White like a bunch of sheep freshly sheared, comin' up clean from the river—each one got a twin, not a gap in sight.
4.3: Your lips got that red ribbon vibe—soft, sweet, speakin' life. Your mouth? Lovely. And your cheeks behind that veil look like a slice of pomegranate—blushin' and beautiful.
4.4: Your neck stand tall like the tower of David, strong, elegant, made to carry honor. Warriors' shields hang from it—you a queen built for battles won.
4.5: Your breasts like twin baby deer, grazin' gentle in a field of lilies—soft, tender, perfectly paired.
4.6: 'Til sunrise breaks and night disappears, I'ma make my way to your mountain of myrrh, and that hill of frankincense. (You know what I mean.)
4.7: Baby girl, you flawless. Ain't a blemish on you anywhere. You all beauty, no doubt.
4.8: Come with me, my bride. Step outta Lebanon with me. Let's climb to the peaks—Amana, Senir, Hermon. Come away from lion dens, from leopard mountains. Come safe with me.
4.9: You got my heart in a chokehold, girl. My queen, my love—One glance from your eyes, one jewel on your chain—and I'm done for.
4.10: Your love? Whew—it hit different. Better than the finest wine. And your scent? It beat every spice on earth.
4.11: When you kiss me? It drip like honeycomb. Milk and honey rest under your tongue. Even your clothes smell like fresh Lebanon air.
4.12: You a whole private garden, sis. Locked up, sacred. A spring no one touched. A sealed-up fountain. You protected and precious.
4.13: Inside you? A whole orchard—pomegranates, sweet fruits, henna blossoms, and spikenard flowin' heavy.
4.14: Spikenard, saffron, calamus, cinnamon—trees pourin' out frankincense, myrrh and aloe—every rich spice a king could ask for.
4.15: You a garden fountain, a fresh spring full of life, water runnin' wild from the mountains of Lebanon.
4.16: Wake up, north wind! Come on, south wind! Blow through my garden, let the fragrance flow. Let my man come in and taste what's his—Let him feast on all this fruit I've been growin'.

5.1: I pulled up in my garden, sis—you know that's mine. Snatched myrrh and spice, scooped up the honeycomb and the honey. Had my wine, poured my milk. To all my people: y'all better eat! Drink up—drink deep, beloveds!
5.2: I was sleepin', but my heart stayed up. Then I heard him knockin'. "My love, my dove, my girl—open up for me. I'm out here drippin' with night dew, my hair wet from waitin'."
5.3: "I done took off my robe—how I'm supposed to put it back on? I already washed my feet—ain't tryna mess 'em up again."
5.4: Then he reached through the latch on the door—And my heart? It jumped. That man got me open.
5.5: I got up quick to let him in. My hands were slick with myrrh, fingers drippin' sweet scent, Right on the lock.
5.6: I opened the door, but he was gone. I felt it deep—he spoke, and it shook me. I ran lookin', but couldn't find him. I called, but he didn't say nothin' back.
5.7: The city guards caught me slippin'. They hit me. Bruised me. Took my veil and left me exposed.
5.8: Y'all, daughters of Jerusalem—if you see my man, Tell him I'm love-sick for real. Like, head over heels.
5.9: Girl, what's so special about your man? Why you so pressed? What make him stand out from everybody else?
5.10: My man? He different. Light-skinned with a glow, deep reddish-brown too—He stand out in a crowd of ten thousand.
5.11: His head? Pure gold. His curls? Laid and black like a raven.
5.12: His eyes be soft like doves chillin' by the riverside—Washed clean, set just right.
5.13: His cheeks? Like gardens full of spice. His lips? Lilies, drippin' with myrrh. I could kiss 'em forever.
5.14: His hands? Solid gold, iced out. His body? Sculpted like ivory, detailed with jewels.
5.15: His legs? Strong like marble columns, Standin' on gold foundations. He carry himself like a cedar tree from Lebanon—noble.
5.16: His mouth? Sweet as honey. Yeah, he all that. That's my man, my friend, So don't ask me twice.

6.1: Girl, where yo' man at? You the baddest of us all—Where he turn off to? We'll help you look for him.
6.2: He out in his garden, Where the spices bloom. Feeding his sheep, Picking lilies like he always do.
6.3: I belong to my man, And he belongs to me. He stay in the lilies—right where I can find him.
6.4: My love, you lookin' like Tirzah—fine and regal. Like Jerusalem herself—majestic, unstoppable, like an army marchin' with flags flyin'.
6.5: Turn your eyes away, girl, You starin' me down too hard. Your gaze? Got me weak. And that hair? Fallin' like goats on a hill in Gilead.
6.6: Your teeth? Still like sheep fresh out the water—all lined up, every one got a twin. No gaps, no stragglers.
6.7: Your cheeks behind that veil? They glow like ripe pomegranate slices. Full of color, full of life.
6.8: Look, I could have sixty queens, eighty side pieces, and virgins without number—
6.9: But you? You my dove. You the one. Only daughter of your mama, Her favorite child. Even the other girls see you and call you blessed—Queens, concubines, all of 'em praise your name.
6.10: Who is she, shinin' like sunrise? Soft like the moonlight, Bright like the noon sun, Standin' strong like a whole army lined up?
6.11: I went out to the valley, Just to check the garden—See if the vines started growin', See if the pomegranates were bloomin'.
6.12: Next thing I know, My spirit lifted me like a royal chariot—Rollin' with my people, feelin' chosen.
6.13: Come back, come back, Shulamite girl! We just wanna see you. Come on back, let us look at you! What y'all lookin' at in me anyway? Is it like watchin' a sacred dance, Like two armies movin' as one?

7.1: Girl, your feet in them sandals? Whew—royalty. You walkin' like a queen. Your thighs curved like they was sculpted by a master. Straight art.
7.2: That belly? Smooth like a goblet, Always full—never lackin'. Your waist? Round and full like a wheat harvest, Surrounded in softness like lilies bloomin'.
7.3: And your breasts? Like two baby deer—Twins of a gazelle, restin' easy.
7.4: Your neck got that regal posture, Like an ivory tower standin' tall. Your eyes? Deep like the pools in Heshbon, Right near the city gate. That nose? Strong and centered—like the tower in Lebanon, Facing Damascus bold.
7.5: That head of yours? Sittin' proud like Mount Carmel. And your hair? Deep purple waves—got a king locked in with just one look.
7.6: You so fine, so pleasant—Everything about you bring joy. I could stare at you for days.
7.7: Your body tall and elegant, Like a palm tree reachin' high. And your breasts? Full like them palm clusters.
7.8: I said to myself, "I'm climbin' that tree. Gonna hold on tight to them branches." Let them curves be like sweet grape clusters, Let your breath smell like fresh-picked apples.
7.9: And your kisses? Whew—like sippin' the finest wine. That wine slide down smooth for my man, Soft on the lips, sweet in his dreams.
7.10: I belong to my love—And he want me just as much as I want him.
7.11: Come on, baby. Let's dip out to the countryside. Let's stay the night somewhere quiet, just you and me.
7.12: Let's wake up early, hit the vineyards, See if the vines startin' to bloom, If the grapes got blossoms, If them pomegranates burstin' open. That's where I'm givin' you all this love.
7.13: The mandrakes got the whole place smellin' right, And by our door? Every kind of fruit—old memories, new moments. I saved it all for you, my love.

8.1: I wish you was like my brother, Somebody I could kiss out in the open, No side eyes, no shame, just love.
8.2: I'd take you by the hand, Bring you into mama's house—The same place I learned how to care. I'd pour you a glass of spiced wine, Let you taste the sweetness of my love.
8.3: His left arm holdin' up my head, His right arm wrapped tight 'round me. That's how we rest.
8.4: I'm tellin' y'all again, daughters of Jerusalem—Don't wake love before it's ready. Let it rise when it wanna rise.
8.5: Who this woman comin' up from the wild, Leanin' on her man like home? I brought you up under that apple tree, Right where your mama birthed you into this world.
8.6: Put me like a tattoo on your heart, Lock me in like a bracelet on your arm. This love? It don't play. It's strong like death, Jealous like the grave, And hot like wildfire. Ain't nothin' lukewarm about it.
8.7: Ain't no flood that can drown it. Ain't no river that can wash it away. If a man tried to buy this love with everything he got? He'd get laughed out the room.
8.8: We got a little sister, She still young, no curves yet. What we gon' do when a man start lookin' at her?
8.9: If she solid like a wall, We'll crown her with silver. If she wide open like a door, We'll frame her in with cedar—lock her in tight.
8.10: Well, I am a wall. And these curves? Yeah, they towerin'. He looked at me and saw peace. Like, finally… this the one.
8.11: Solomon got a vineyard out in Baal Hamon, He leased it out, made folks pay for the fruit—A thousand silver coins just for what grows.
8.12: But my vineyard? That's mine. You, Solomon, can keep your thousands, Let the workers get their cut. But what I got? Priceless. I ain't for sale.
8.13: You out there in the gardens, Everybody listenin' for your voice—Let me be the one to hear it.
8.14: Come on, baby. Run to me like a gazelle, Fast and free, On the hills that smell like home.
